summary: Burst of 503s traced to prefetch-lock amplification causing upstream runtime crashloops and API gateway timeouts
description: Issue summary: Between 2026-03-10 02:15 and 2026-03-10 03:40 UTC Waveform AI experienced a sudden elevated 5xx rate (primarily 503) from the Redwood hosted API. Impact: customer streaming sessions failed with repeated 503s and client-side disconnects; several hundred requests failed per minute. Environment: dedicated tenant on prod us-west serving gptk-13b-quant. Initial triage suggested API gateway timeouts; deeper inspection shows upstream serving runtimes repeatedly crashing/restarting under a prefetch lock amplification scenario.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate sustained streaming burst from single-tenant (Waveform AI) with ~120 concurrent streaming sessions sending small prompts (avg 30 tokens) and prefetched model variant enabled. 2) Observe runtime prefetch subsystem queuing and increased lock contention on kv-cache shard 7. 3) After ~90s of sustained burst, upstream runtimes begin failing healthchecks and restart, API gateway returns 503/502 to callers. 4) Increasing the burst concurrency reproduces the crashloop more rapidly. Note: behavior not reproduced on lighter workloads or with prefetch disabled.

2026-03-10T02:19:07Z runtime[pid=2451] ERROR watchdog: worker OOM? exit_code=137 kernel_message=Killed process 2451 (runtime)
investigation_notes: - Customer reported sudden increase in error rate at 02:15 UTC; support confirmed spike in 503s correlated to Waveform AI tenant. - SRE pulled runtime logs and noticed high prefetch queue lengths and long lock wait times localized to kv-cache shard 7. - Memory metrics: GPU memory utilization remained stable; CPU and thread contention spiked. - Autoscaler logs show no scale-up events during the first 2 minutes of the burst due to conservative HPA thresholds. - Reproduced locally in staging by replaying customer traffic pattern; disabling prefetch prevented crashloop. - Hypothesis: prefetch subsystem acquires a shard-level lock during model prefetch; with many concurrent small streaming sessions the prefetch hot-path serializes work and starves runtime main threads, causing healthcheck failures and ultimately runtime restarts. - Related findings: a similar prefetch lock amplification was referenced in SUP-328765 but that incident involved different shard skew; here amplification is tenant-local and tied to streaming keepalive patterns.
comments: 2026-03-10 02:42 - Support (Priya): Acknowledge customer, asked for request IDs and whether they had pinned model variants. Customer confirmed model pinning and streaming-heavy workloads.

2026-03-10 03:05 - SRE (Ethan): Collected runtime core dumps and kv-cache shard metrics; opened a short Slack thread #support-prefetch (https://slack.redwood/threads/T12345) and posted initial observations.
2026-03-10 03:22 - Customer (Waveform AI, T. Alvarez): Provided sample request IDs and agreed to test a temporary mitigation (disable prefetch on tenant).

2026-03-10 03:40 - Support (Priya): Applied tenant-level config to disable prefetch; customer reported error rate dropping to baseline within ~2 minutes. Proceeding with mitigation rollout and root cause analysis.
2026-03-11 09:15 - Eng (Sophie Chen): Noted potential quick patch: reduce lock scope in prefetch codepath and add shard-aware backoff. Follow-up PR planned.
2026-03-12 11:00 - SRE (Ethan): Increased autoscaler sensitivity for dedicated tenants and scheduled a controlled rollout of kv-cache shard rebalancer to prevent shard skew under tenant bursts.
resolution: Workaround applied: tenant-level prefetch disabled for Waveform AI at 2026-03-10 03:40 UTC which immediately reduced 503s. Mitigations in flight: 1) Hotfix PR to narrow prefetch lock scope and add exponential backoff (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4521). 2) Autoscaler policy adjusted to allow faster scale-up on tenant-specific streaming CPU-thread pressure. 3) Short-term operational change: monitor kv-cache shard hotness and trigger automated shard rebalancer when shard queue length > 200 for >60s. Follow-ups: full postmortem due 2026-03-17, test case added to chaos/stress suite covering tenant-local prefetch bursts, and customer follow-up call scheduled for 2026-03-13.

SRE-2: Implement shard hotness alert and automated rebalancer rule by 2026-03-16
